info.title: Hikyaku Logistics API
info.description:
Backend for the Hikyaku dashboard and the public booking site.

**Authentication.** Every route except the public booking and routing endpoints requires a Supabase access token as `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`.

**Tenancy.** Authenticated routes resolve the active organisation from the `X-Organisation-Slug` header. The unauthenticated booking and routing routes read `x-org-slug` instead — a separate header, not a casing variant. Each operation declares the one it expects.

**Errors.** Failures use Nest’s default body (`{ statusCode, message, error }`); `message` is an array of strings when request validation is what failed. See `ApiErrorDto`.

statusCode.description: Mirrors the HTTP status code of the response.

message.description: A single message for a hand-thrown exception, or one entry per failed constraint when request validation is what rejected the call.

error.description: HTTP reason phrase for the status code.

coordinates.description: Position as [lon, lat] — GeoJSON order, not [lat, lon].

osm_type.description: OSM element type: N, W or R.

name.description: Primary display name of the result.

extent.description: Bounding box as [minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat].

warehouse_id.description: UUID of the warehouse the driver belongs to

license_type.description: UUID FK to vehicle_type.id (the driver license class)

user_role.description: Role name, must match an existing app_roles.name

user_id.description: Supabase auth id of the invited user.

user_role.description: Role name, echoed from the request.

user_permission.description: The granted permissions as a JSON-encoded string array, not an array — `JSON.parse` before use. Deduplicated against the request.

invited_at.description: When the invitation email was issued.

user_avatar_upload_url.description: Short-lived signed URL for uploading the avatar directly to storage. Present only when the request set `user_avatar` — image bytes never pass through this API.

user_ids.description: Users to deactivate. Each is processed independently — see the response’s `failed` array rather than assuming all-or-nothing. The caller cannot deactivate themselves, and accounts holding every permission are refused.

reason.description: Human-readable cause, e.g. "Cannot deactivate your own account". For display only — do not branch on the text.

deactivated.description: Users banned and signed out of every session.

failed.description: Users left untouched, with the reason for each.

user_ids.description: Users to lift the deactivation ban from. Each is processed independently — see the response’s `failed` array.

reactivated.description: Users whose deactivation ban was lifted.

failed.description: Users left untouched, with the reason for each.

user_id.description: The team member whose role changes. Must already belong to the organisation resolved from `X-Organisation-Slug`.

role_name.description: Role name, must match an existing app_roles.name — e.g. `Driver`. An unknown name is rejected with 400.

role.description: The role now in effect, resolved from the requested name.

peliasGid.description: Pelias global id for stable re-lookup

stripe_customer_id.description: Linked Stripe customer on the organisation’s connected account. Null until the organisation enables payments, and null if the best-effort Stripe sync failed.

shopify_customer_id.description: Set only for customers created from a Shopify order.

customer_name.description: Empty string when the column is null, never null itself.

customer_phone.description: E.164 where known. Empty string when unset.

customer_address.description: Street line. Empty string when unset.

geocode_confidence.description: Pelias geocode confidence (0–1). Only set for addresses entered through the geocoded manual-entry form.

pelias_gid.description: Pelias global id, for stable re-lookup of the address.

pelias_raw.description: Raw Pelias feature kept for provenance. Opaque — do not read fields off it.

data.description: One page of customers, newest first. Shorter than `pageSize` on the last page, and empty past the end.

total.description: Total customers in the organisation, ignoring pagination — divide by `pageSize` for the page count.

state.description: `none` — no trial applies to this organisation, which is the case for personal orgs and for orgs created before trials existed. They are unrestricted, NOT expired. `active` — trial running. `expired` — the deadline has passed and tenant-scoped endpoints answer 402.

trialEndsAt.description: ISO 8601 instant the trial ends, or null when `state` is `none`. Returned raw so the dashboard can render it in the viewer’s locale.

daysRemaining.description: Whole days remaining, floored — so the final day reads 0, not 1. Null when `state` is `none`, and 0 rather than negative once expired.

shiftsUsedThisPeriod.description: Shifts created by this organisation so far this calendar month.

freeAllowance.description: Shifts included before overage billing applies. PLACEHOLDER — see create-stripe-subscriptions.ps1 for the actual figure per org type.

hasPaymentMethod.description: Whether the organisation has a payment method on file. Once `shiftsUsedThisPeriod` reaches `freeAllowance`, further shift creation is blocked (HTTP 400 / check_violation) unless this is true.

periodEnd.description: ISO 8601 instant the free allowance resets (start of next calendar month).

hasVanityUrlEntitlement.description: Whether the organisation is currently entitled to a vanity booking subdomain (<vanity_slug>.hikyaku.org). True for a grandfathered company org unconditionally, otherwise mirrors the live vanity_url Stripe entitlement synced from that org's Billing customer.

returnUrl.description: Where Stripe redirects the browser after the customer leaves the Billing Portal — typically the page the "Add payment method" button was clicked from.

url.description: Stripe-hosted Billing Portal URL to redirect the browser to.

id.description: Client-supplied packages.id. Both clients mint a UUID before the call so they can name the storage path for photos; supplying it here keeps that working and makes the create idempotent on replay. Omitted, the server generates one.

warehouseId.description: warehouse.id the package is dispatched from. Must belong to the active organisation.

toCustomerId.description: customer.id of the recipient. Its customer_location is the routed stop; a recipient with no geocode cannot be assigned.

trackingNumber.description: Human-facing tracking number. Omitted, the packages_set_tracking_number trigger generates one. Re-sending an existing number with an identical payload replays the original package instead of creating a second.

deadlineAt.description: Hard deadline — the promise made to the customer, stored in package_delivery_window.scheduled_arrival and never overwritten by the planner. Packages WITHOUT a deadline are the ones eligible to be bumped off a shift to make room for one that has a deadline.

autoAssign.description: Run assignment immediately after creation. The mobile create-shift wizard MUST send false: it creates packages then hands their ids to POST /api/v1/optimisation/adhoc, which rejects a package that already belongs to an optimisation.

deadlineAt.description: The hard deadline (package_delivery_window.scheduled_arrival). Null means the package has no promise and may be bumped to make room.

status.description: Latest package_timeline status enum, e.g. PENDING, ASSIGNED.

id.description: vrp_optimization.id — a shift is a vrp_optimization row.

stopIndex.description: Zero-based position of this package among the route job steps, excluding the depot start/end steps.

estimatedArrival.description: Planner ETA (package_delivery_window.estimated_arrival). Rewritten on every replan; never a deadline.

revision.description: vrp_optimization.revision at the time of assignment. Clients compare this against GET /api/v1/shifts/{id}/version to detect a replan.

outcome.description: `assigned` — joined an existing planned shift. `assigned_new_shift` — a new shift was opened for it, which consumes one shift from the organisation allowance. `deferred` — created but not assigned; it will be picked up by the next replan or by a dispatcher. `skipped` — assignment was not attempted.

evictedPackageIds.description: Packages bumped off a shift to make room for this one. Each was re-assigned in the same request where possible; any that could not be are back at PENDING. Empty in the normal case.

index.description: Index into the submitted packages array.

error.description: Failure detail for this entry. One bad entry does not fail the batch.

driverId.description: Driver (user) id to issue the card to

vehicleId.description: Vehicle to associate the card with

spendingLimitMajor.description: Major-unit spend cap, e.g. 150 for $150.00. Omit for no card-level limit.

currency.description: ISO currency matching the platform Stripe account (usd/eur/gbp)

id.description: Stripe card id — the same value as `stripeCardId`.

cardholderId.description: Stripe cardholder id for the driver. Empty string in the unlikely case Stripe returned no cardholder.

vehicleId.description: Vehicle the card is associated with, from Stripe card metadata. Null when the card was issued without one.

stripeCardId.description: Stripe card id. Duplicates `id`; kept for clarity at call sites.

last4.description: Last four digits of the PAN. The full number never leaves Stripe.

type.description: Always `virtual` — physical cards are not issued.

spendingLimitMinor.description: Spend cap in minor units for the interval below. Null when the card carries no card-level limit.

spendingInterval.description: Window the limit resets over. Null when there is no limit.

updatedAt.description: Stripe exposes no update timestamp on cards, so this mirrors `createdAt` to keep the shape stable. Do not treat it as a real modification time.

id.description: Stripe transaction id — the same value as `stripeTransactionId`.

vehicleId.description: From the card’s Stripe metadata; null if the card has no vehicle.

stripeAuthorizationId.description: The authorization this transaction settled, where there was one.

type.description: Anything Stripe does not report as a refund is a capture.

amountMinor.description: Magnitude in minor units, always positive. Stripe reports spend as a negative amount; the sign is dropped here, so use `type` to tell a refund from a capture.

authorizedAt.description: Mirrors `createdAt` — Stripe exposes one timestamp here.

apiVersion.description: Stripe API version pinned by the client SDK

ephemeralKeySecret.description: Short-lived Stripe ephemeral key secret. Pass it straight to Issuing Elements to render full card details client-side — the PAN never touches this server. Do not log or persist it.

clientSecret.description: Account Session client secret for @stripe/connect-js. Single-use and short-lived — fetch a fresh one per mount rather than caching it.

publishableKey.description: The platform’s Stripe publishable key, returned so the frontend need not carry it separately.

accountId.description: Connected account id, or null before onboarding begins.

detailsSubmitted.description: Whether the org finished Stripe’s onboarding form.

chargesEnabled.description: Whether the account can take payments. Gates the service-rates and booking features.

payoutsEnabled.description: Whether Stripe will pay out to the account.

cardIssuingStatus.description: Stripe capability state — `active`, `pending`, `inactive`, or null when never requested. Fuel cards need `active`.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country, fixed at account creation and immutable afterwards.

cardIssuingStatus.description: As on the status endpoint. Null when the org has no account.

chargesEnabled.description: Whether the connected account can accept payments — gates "Service Rates".

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the receiving bank.

type.description: Transfer rail, derived from the account currency — one of `us_bank_transfer`, `gb_bank_transfer`, `eu_bank_transfer`.

financial_addresses.description: Bank coordinates to wire to. The fields vary by rail — ACH exposes routing and account numbers, SEPA an IBAN — so this is left opaque rather than modelled per country. Render it, do not branch on it.

currency.description: Lower-case ISO 4217 code the account is funded in.

amount.description: Available to spend, in minor units. Can be zero, and is not the account’s payments balance — Issuing funds are held separately.

org_id.description: Id of the organisation to invite into. Must be the same organisation the `X-Organisation-Slug` header resolves to — a mismatch is rejected with 400. Redundant by design: it makes the caller state which tenant they believe they are acting on.

role.description: Role name, must match an existing app_roles.name

id.description: The invitation row. Re-inviting an address that already has an outstanding invitation updates that one and returns its existing id rather than creating a second.

email.description: Lower-cased — compare case-insensitively against the request.

status.description: Always `pending`: the invitation exists but has not been acted on. The email is sent best-effort afterwards, so a 201 does not confirm delivery.

role.description: Role the invitee is granted on acceptance.

permissions.description: Permissions granted alongside the role. Empty when the invitation carries none.

organisation_slug.description: Slug of the joined organisation — switch the active tenant to it. Empty string in the unlikely case the organisation row has since gone.

ok.description: Always true — a failure to decline surfaces as a 404, never as `false`.

amountMajor.description: Per-unit rate in major units (e.g. dollars).

currency.description: ISO currency code; defaults to the account default.

id.description: Stripe product id of the created or updated item. Stable across price edits.

amountMajor.description: Per-unit rate in major units (e.g. dollars).
Per-unit rate in major units (e.g. dollars).
Per-unit rate in major units (e.g. dollars).

id.description: Stripe product id — the stable public handle for this item. Editing a price mints a new Stripe price but leaves this unchanged.

pricing_unit.description: How the booking quantity is derived at quote time. Read from Stripe product metadata, defaulting to `per_delivery` when absent.

amount_minor.description: Per-unit rate in the currency’s minor units, e.g. 1250 for $12.50. The line total is this multiplied by the derived quantity.

id.description: Stripe product id — the stable public handle for this item. Editing a price mints a new Stripe price but leaves this unchanged.

pricing_unit.description: How the booking quantity is derived at quote time. Read from Stripe product metadata, defaulting to `per_delivery` when absent.

amount_minor.description: Per-unit rate in the currency’s minor units, e.g. 1250 for $12.50. The line total is this multiplied by the derived quantity.

addons.description: Add-ons belonging to this service, oldest first. Only these are accepted in `addonIds` when quoting or paying for it.

services.description: The organisation’s bookable services, oldest first. Empty when the organisation has not connected a Stripe account, or when no `x-org-slug` was supplied.

id.description: Stripe product id of the service or add-on this line bills.

rate.description: Per-unit rate in major units (e.g. dollars), for display beside the quantity. Derived from the Stripe price.

quantity.description: Units billed, derived server-side from the booking: 1 for `per_delivery`, the recipient count for `per_recipient`, and the measured route distance or parcel weight otherwise. Fractional for the distance and weight units.

amount_minor.description: Line total in minor units — `rate × quantity`, rounded.

currency.description: Lower-case ISO 4217 code shared by every line, taken from the first line. Falls back to `usd` for an empty quote.

lines.description: The chosen service first, then each selected add-on in the order it was requested.

total.description: `total_minor` expressed in major units, for display. Never use it to reconcile against Stripe — `total_minor` is the exact figure.

deliveryNotes.description: Free-text notes shown to the driver.

checkoutUrl.description: Stripe-hosted Checkout URL. Redirect the browser to it — do not fetch or embed it.

sessionId.description: Checkout Session id, echoed back to the success URL as `session_id` so the confirmation page can identify the booking.

coordinates.description: Stops to route through, as [lng, lat] pairs in visit order.
Whole-route path as [lng, lat] pairs, legs concatenated with shared boundary points de-duplicated.

wayPoints.description: Index into `coordinates` of each stop. wayPoints[0] is 0 and the last entry is coordinates.length - 1.

legs.description: Per stop-pair legs — n stops yield n-1 legs.

setOffAt.description: ISO timestamp the vehicle should set off.

optimisationId.description: vrp_optimization.id once the run has produced one.

error.description: Failure detail when status is `failed`, or the reason no packages were eligible when status is `skipped`. Always null otherwise.

nextAllowedAt.description: Earliest time another run is allowed. Null when this run does not count toward the rate limit (failed or skipped).

startDateTime.description: ISO-8601 timestamp the vehicle sets off.

driverId.description: drivers.id — the driver this shift is assigned to. Must share a warehouse with vehicleId.

vehicleId.description: vehicles.id — the vehicle this shift is assigned to; also resolves the routing profile via vehicles.vehicle_type. Must share a warehouse with driverId.

packages.description: Existing packages.id values to deliver on this shift. Each must sit at startingLocationId and not already belong to another optimisation.

routeId.description: vrp_route.id of the single routed vehicle, or null when VROOM produced no route.

unassignedPackageIds.description: Requested packages VROOM could not fit into the shift. Empty when every package was assigned.

warehouseId.description: warehouse.id the shift starts and ends at.

driverId.description: drivers.id. Must share a warehouse with vehicleId.

vehicleId.description: vehicles.id. Also resolves the routing profile via vehicles.vehicle_type.

shiftDate.description: Warehouse-local service day (YYYY-MM-DD). A driver or vehicle can hold at most one open shift per day.

scheduledStart.description: When the vehicle sets off. Omitted, the shift stays open to automatic assignment indefinitely; set, it closes 15 minutes before this time so nothing is added to a van about to roll.

status.description: `planned` is the only state open to automatic assignment, and only until 15 minutes before scheduledStart.

routeId.description: vrp_route.id of the single route, or null while the shift is empty.

stopCount.description: Job steps on the route, excluding depot start/end.

revision.description: Compare against the loaded value; differs means replan.

packageIds.description: Existing packages.id values. Candidate selection is bypassed, but feasibility still runs: a package that breaks a deadline is reported as a warning rather than refused.

added.description: False when the package was already claimed elsewhere.

warning.description: Set when the package was added but breaks something — e.g. its own deadline, or another stop’s. The dispatcher decided; we record it.

populated.description: Live check: whether tzdata.timezone currently has rows. Authoritative regardless of whether this instance ran the import itself.

importState.description: What this instance has observed/done for the background boot-time import.

updatedAt.description: ISO timestamp of the last state transition on this instance.

status.description: Always "ok" — the endpoint only reports process liveness.
